title: A point with values in a field lying over the image of an immersion factors through it
statement: Let $\iota:Z\to X$ be an immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-closed-immersion] (a closed immersion $Z\to W$ followed by an open immersion $W\to X$), let $z\in Z$ and $x=\iota(z)$. (1) The map $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(z)$ induced by $\iota$ on residue fields [def-weil-residue-field] is an isomorphism. (2) Let $K$ be a field and $s:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] a morphism of schemes mapping the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ to $x$. Then there is exactly one morphism $s':\operatorname{Spec}K\to Z$ with $\iota\circ s'=s$, and $s'$ maps the unique point to $z$. In particular, if $\bar x=s$ is a geometric point of $X$ [def-weil-geometric-point] lying over a point of $\iota(Z)$, then $\bar x=\iota\circ\bar z$ for a unique geometric point $\bar z:\operatorname{Spec}K\to Z$ (with the same algebraically closed field $K$).

source.place: Schemes, Definition 01IO (definition-immersion, line 1781: (5) immersion = closed immersion followed by open immersion), Definition 01HK (definition-closed-immersion-locally-ringed-spaces, line 344: O_X -> i_*O_Z surjective), the discussion before Lemma 01J9 (lemma-characterize-points, lines 2420-2475: morphisms Spec(K) -> X correspond to pairs (x, kappa(x) -> K)), and Lemma 01L7 (lemma-immersions-monomorphisms, line 4639) for uniqueness

proof.text: *Residue fields.* By the definition of an immersion, write $\iota=o\circ c$ with $c:Z\to W$ a closed immersion and $o:W\to X$ an open immersion. The map $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(c(z))$ induced by $o$ is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality], and the map $\kappa(c(z))\to\kappa(z)$ induced by $c$ is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-residue-field-iso].

source.place: Schemes, Definition Tag 01IO and Definition Tag 01HK, with the residue-field discussion before Lemma Tag 01J9

proof.text: The residue-field map induced by the composite $\iota=o\circ c$ is the composite of the two maps in Step 1, because the local homomorphisms on stalks and their residue maps compose. A composite of isomorphisms is an isomorphism, proving (1).

source.place: Schemes, the commutative residue-field diagram in the discussion before Lemma Tag 01J9

proof.text: *Existence of the lift.* Keep the factorization $\iota=o\circ c$ from Step 1. Since the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ maps under $s$ to $x=o(c(z))\in o(W)$, [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] gives a unique $t:\operatorname{Spec}K\to W$ with $o\circ t=s$. The point of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ maps under $t$ to $c(z)$. The new statement [lem-weil-pbc-field-point-factors-through-closed-immersion] therefore gives a unique $s':\operatorname{Spec}K\to Z$ with $c\circ s'=t$, and its point is $z$. Thus $\iota\circ s'=s$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma Tag 01HI, Lemma Tag 0356, and Definition Tag 01IO

proof.text: *Uniqueness and geometric points.* If $u:\operatorname{Spec}K\to Z$ also satisfies $\iota\circ u=s$, the monomorphism $o$ gives $c\circ u=t$; the uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-field-point-factors-through-closed-immersion] gives $u=s'$. For an algebraically closed $K$, this is exactly the stated factorization of a geometric point, with the same field.

lean.statement: theorem fieldPoint_factorsThrough_immersion {Z X : Scheme.{u}} (iota : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion iota] (z : Z) : IsIso (iota.residueFieldMap z) ∧ ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] (s : Spec (.of K) ⟶ X), s.base ((default : Spec (.of K))) = iota.base z → (∃! s' : Spec (.of K) ⟶ Z, s' ≫ iota = s) ∧ ∀ s' : Spec (.of K) ⟶ Z, s' ≫ iota = s → s'.base ((default : Spec (.of K))) = z
